t.p: This connects one Shopify store to this Odoo database. It takes about ten minutes, and nothing synchronizes and nothing is written to Shopify until you finish and say so.

ul.li: Admin access to your Shopify organization, so you can create an app for this store in the Dev Dashboard and copy its Client ID and Client secret — or an Admin API access token you already hold from an app created the older way. Either path works; the credential step explains both.
About ten minutes. You can stop at any point and pick up where you left off.

div.div: This connector needs Odoo.sh or on-premise hosting
Odoo Online (SaaS) cannot run it, because the connector needs background workers and outbound calls that Odoo Online does not provide. Better to know now than at the last step.

t.p: Name this store so you recognise it later, and point it at the right Shopify shop.

div.label: Shopify domain
div.small: Your store's permanent address, ending in .myshopify.com. Find it in Shopify under Settings → Domains. We confirm it against Shopify at the readiness step — we don't take it on trust here.

t.p: One Shopify store per setup. Connecting a second shop means a second store here.
Choose how this store authenticates with Shopify, then enter that path's credentials. If a credential is already on record, leave the fields blank to keep it.

label.span: Dev Dashboard app (Client ID and secret)
For an app created in Shopify's Dev Dashboard. Odoo exchanges these for an access token and renews it automatically — Shopify does not show you a token to copy on this path.
For a store that already holds a long-lived Admin API access token from an app created the older way.

div.div: Both values are on your app's Overview page in the Dev Dashboard

This works only when the app and the store belong to the same Shopify organization. The token Shopify issues lasts 24 hours; Odoo requests a fresh one before it expires, so there is nothing to renew by hand. Shopify's guide: Get API access tokens (Dev Dashboard).

div.label: Client ID
div.small: The app's public identifier. Shopify shows it beside the Client secret.

div.label: Client secret
div.small: Stored behind administrator-only access and never shown again — not here, not in the store form, not in a log. Rotate it in the Dev Dashboard if it is ever exposed.

div.div: This path needs the Admin API access token — not the Client ID, and not the Client Secret

An older-style custom app shows all three. The Admin API access token is the one that goes in the field below. If your app only shows a Client ID and Client secret, use the Dev Dashboard path above instead.
How long a token stays valid depends on how it was issued. Check your Shopify app's authentication method rather than assuming a fixed lifetime.

div.label: Admin API access token
div.small: Stored behind administrator-only access and never shown again — not here, not in the store form, not in a log. If you lose it, create a new one in Shopify and paste that.

t.p: A credential is already on record for this store (Dev Dashboard app) (access token). Leave this path's fields blank to keep it. Enter new values to replace it; changing the path also requires new values, and the connection has to be tested again.

div.div: Secrets entered here are write-only
They are protected by access control, not by encryption at rest. Anyone with database access can read them, so treat database backups as containing them.

t.p: These are the permissions the connector needs, and why. You grant them in Shopify when you create the custom app — this screen does not grant anything. We verify them at the readiness step.
This makes one read-only call to Shopify to prove the credentials work. Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

Go back one step and re-enter the Client ID and Client secret from your app's page in the Dev Dashboard. Check that the app belongs to the same Shopify organization as this store, and check the shop domain.
Go back one step and paste the token again — check that you copied the Admin API access token and not the Client ID or Client Secret — or check the shop domain.

t.p: Choose what this connector does. Enabling nothing is a valid choice — a connected store that syncs nothing yet is fine.

t.p: Match each Shopify location to the Odoo internal location that manages its stock. Locations are loaded automatically, and every active Shopify location must be mapped before you continue. Nothing is matched by name.

t.p: Two decisions with real consequences, and no default. Both are required.

fieldset.legend: Which system is the source for your catalog?
Which system is the price authority?

t.p: Leaving the price authority with Shopify means prices are never exported. That block is stated here so it is never a surprise later.
Right now, customers will not be emailed when a delivery is fulfilled. Re-run guided Setup to change this explicitly confirmed choice.

label.span: Let Shopify email my customers about fulfillments

div.div: Shopify will email your customers
Every delivery you validate in Odoo will send a Shopify shipping notification to that order's customer.

label.span: I understand, and I want customers emailed

t.p: Nothing is written to Shopify until you review and confirm the stock preview. Stock scanning is enabled automatically so the preview is ready when product mappings exist.

div.div: First stock push is protected

Odoo is the inventory authority. The connector reads Shopify available quantity only for comparison and prepares the exact Odoo quantity that would be written for each mapped product and location. Shopify stock is never imported into Odoo. An Administrator must confirm every first push before any quantity can be sent.
Not required
Inventory syncing is not enabled for this store, so there is no first stock push to schedule. You can enable it later in Sync Rules, and this step will be waiting.

t.p: Everything known to break a first sync, checked against the choices you have just made. Each result says what it means, who fixes it, and whether it blocks activation.

t.p: Activation starts the selected read and import scans and reconciles Shopify webhook subscriptions. It does not itself export catalog, inventory, or fulfillment business data. Later writes follow each domain's safeguards, including preview and confirmation where applicable. The dashboard shows initial synchronization progress, exceptions, and the next required action.
